youtube.aciklama:
How are the gain, maximum output and frequency response of a hearing aid defined and measured? In this lesson we use the ANSI S3.22 definitions to cover OSPL90, full-on gain, the reference test setting, frequency range, harmonic distortion and equivalent input noise.

AIHEAR Audiology Academy makes short, clear lessons for audiology students and professionals.

Sources: ANSI/ASA S3.22, Specification of Hearing Aid Characteristics; IEC 60118 series, Electroacoustics: Hearing aids; Dillon, Hearing Aids; Stelmachowicz et al., Effect of stimulus bandwidth on the perception of /s/ in normal- and hearing-impaired children and adults, Journal of the Acoustical Society of America (2001); Katz, Handbook of Clinical Audiology.

This video is for educational purposes and does not replace diagnosis or treatment.

cumleler: Hello, and welcome to the AIHEAR Audiology Academy.
In this lesson we will learn how to define and measure the gain, maximum output and frequency response of a hearing aid.
We will also cover quality measures such as harmonic distortion and equivalent input noise, as defined in the standards.

maddeler.metin: Does the aid match manufacturer data?
Measured in a 2 cc coupler, test box

cumleler: Electroacoustic measurements show whether a hearing aid matches the characteristics reported by the manufacturer.
Before a new aid is delivered, and when there is a complaint of malfunction, these measurements provide quality control.

cumleler.yazi: In the US these measurements follow the ANSI S3.22 standard, and internationally the IEC 60118 series of standards.
cumleler.ses: In the U.S. these measurements follow the ANSI S three point twenty two standard, and internationally the I E C sixty one eighteen series of standards.

cumleler.yazi: The measurement is done in a soundproof test box, with the aid connected to a standard coupler with a volume of 2 cc.
cumleler.ses: The measurement is done in a soundproof test box, with the aid connected to a standard coupler with a volume of two cc.

cumleler: A coupler is not an ear, so the results show the aid's own characteristics, not its performance in the person's ear.
Before measuring, adaptive features such as noise reduction and feedback management are switched off.
The aid is measured in omnidirectional microphone mode, at the widest frequency response and highest output setting.
The most basic concept is gain: how many decibels the aid adds to the sound.
Gain is found by subtracting the input level from the output level.

cumleler.yazi: In this example graph, the aid receives an input of 60 dB SPL at every frequency.
The output measured in the coupler at 1600 Hz is 101 dB SPL, so the gain at this frequency is 41 decibels.
cumleler.ses: The output measured in the coupler at sixteen hundred hertz is one hundred one decibels SPL, so the gain at this frequency is forty one decibels.

cumleler: Gain varies with frequency; in this aid it is lower at low and very high frequencies.

cumleler.yazi: To summarize it in a single number, the standard uses the high-frequency average, or HFA.
cumleler.ses: To summarize it in a single number, the standard uses the high-frequency average, or H F A.

cumleler.yazi: HFA is the average of the values at 1000, 1600 and 2500 Hz; the manufacturer may also define three other frequencies.
cumleler.ses: H F A is the average of the values at one thousand, sixteen hundred and twenty five hundred hertz; the manufacturer may also define three other frequencies.

cumleler.yazi: The standard measure of maximum output is OSPL90: the output sound pressure level in the coupler for a 90 dB SPL input.
cumleler.ses: The standard measure of maximum output is O S P L ninety: the output sound pressure level in the coupler for a ninety decibel SPL input.

cumleler: In this measurement, the aid's gain is turned fully on and the frequency is swept.
With gain fully on, a ninety decibel input drives most aids to their output limit, that is, into saturation.
So the curve shows the highest sound level the aid can deliver at each frequency.

cumleler.yazi: In this example, the curve peaks at 1600 Hz, at about 118 dB SPL.
cumleler.ses: In this example, the curve peaks at sixteen hundred hertz, at about one hundred eighteen decibels SPL.

cumleler.yazi: The average at 1000, 1600 and 2500 hertz is reported as HFA-OSPL90; here about 116 dB SPL.
cumleler.ses: The average at one thousand, sixteen hundred and twenty five hundred hertz is reported as H F A O S P L ninety; here about one hundred sixteen decibels SPL.

cumleler: The standard sets a tolerance of plus or minus 4 decibels for this average, relative to the manufacturer's value.
In the clinic, maximum output is set so that it does not exceed the person's loudness discomfort level.
Full-on gain is the gain measured with a 50 dB SPL input while the gain control is at maximum.
It is reported as a high-frequency average and has a tolerance of plus or minus 5 decibels relative to the manufacturer's value.
Most other measurements are made at the reference test setting, with a 60 dB SPL input.

cumleler.yazi: At this setting, gain is adjusted so that HFA gain equals HFA-OSPL90 minus 77 decibels, within plus or minus 1.5 decibels.
cumleler.ses: At this setting, gain is adjusted so that H F A gain equals H F A O S P L ninety minus seventy seven decibels, within plus or minus one point five decibels.

cumleler: If the aid's full-on gain cannot reach this value, the reference setting is the full-on position.
The logic of this rule is simple: a sixty decibel input produces an output 17 decibels below the maximum output.
So the aid is tested in a working range similar to everyday use, without saturating during the measurement.
The frequency response is gain plotted against frequency at the reference test setting, with a 60 dB SPL input.
In this example, the high-frequency average is about 39 decibels.
The standard defines the frequency range with a line drawn 20 decibels below this average.

cumleler.yazi: The lowest frequency where the response curve crosses this line is called f1, and the highest is called f2.
cumleler.ses: The lowest frequency where the response curve crosses this line is called F one, and the highest is called F two.

cumleler: In this example, the frequency range is about 300 Hz to 5400 Hz.
The measured curve must stay within plus or minus 4 decibels of the manufacturer's curve at low and mid frequencies, 6 at high ones.
This is the range in the coupler; in the ear canal, the response differs depending on the earmold and vent.
The energy of fricative consonants in speech, such as s and sh, lies mostly at high frequencies.
Especially for female and child talkers, the energy of the s sound extends above 4000 Hz.

cumleler.yazi: Studies by Stelmachowicz and colleagues showed that children need a wide bandwidth to learn these sounds.
cumleler.ses: Studies by Stelmakovich and colleagues showed that children need a wide bandwidth to learn these sounds.

cumleler: In English, grammatical markers such as plurals and possessives are carried by these sounds, so language learning can be affected.
A wide bandwidth also helps music and environmental sounds sound more natural.
In practice, high-frequency gain is often limited by receiver power and acoustic feedback.
A healthy aid only amplifies an incoming pure tone; a faulty aid adds new frequencies to the sound.
These new components appear at exact multiples of the input frequency and are called harmonics.
Total harmonic distortion, or THD, is the ratio of the total power of the harmonics to the fundamental.
This ratio is given as a percentage.

cumleler.yazi: In this example, next to the 500 Hz fundamental, two harmonics appear at 1000 and 1500 Hz.

cumleler: The second harmonic is about 30 decibels below the fundamental; on its own, this corresponds to about 3 percent distortion.

cumleler.yazi: In the standard, the measurement is made at 500, 800 and 1600 Hz with a 70 dB SPL input; at the highest frequency the input is 65 dB SPL.

cumleler: The measured value may exceed the manufacturer's value by at most 3 percent; high THD suggests a weak battery or a damaged receiver.

maddeler.metin: Audible in quiet and open fits

cumleler: Every hearing aid produces a small amount of noise from its microphone and circuits, even with no input.
Equivalent input noise expresses this internal noise as if it were an external sound at the input.

cumleler.yazi: The calculation: the HFA gain for a 50 dB SPL input is subtracted from the noise level measured in the coupler with no input.
cumleler.ses: The calculation: the H F A gain for a fifty decibel SPL input is subtracted from the noise level measured in the coupler with no input.

cumleler.yazi: For example, if the output noise is 58 dB SPL and the gain is 38 decibels, the equivalent input noise is 20 dB SPL.

cumleler: The measured value may exceed the manufacturer's value by at most 3 decibels.
People with near-normal low-frequency hearing may hear this noise as a hiss, especially in quiet settings and with an open fit.
Battery current is measured at the reference setting with a 1000 Hz, 65 dB SPL input, and tells us about battery life.
It may exceed the manufacturer's value by at most 20 percent; high current can explain a battery that runs down faster than expected.
In aids with a telecoil, the telecoil response is measured with a source that simulates the magnetic field of a telephone.
In compression aids, the input-output curve is plotted from 50 to 90 dB SPL in 5 decibel steps.
Attack and release times are also measured by suddenly changing the input level.
We will cover these last two measurements in detail in the next lesson on compression.

cumleler.yazi: Now let us see the measurements together: maximum output uses a 90 dB SPL input, and HFA-OSPL90 has a tolerance of plus or minus 4 decibels.
cumleler.ses: Now let us see the measurements together: maximum output uses a ninety decibel SPL input, and H F A O S P L ninety has a tolerance of plus or minus four decibels.

cumleler: Full-on gain is measured with a 50 dB SPL input and has a tolerance of plus or minus 5 decibels.
Frequency response is measured with a 60 dB SPL input; the tolerance is 4 to 6 decibels depending on the frequency region.
Harmonic distortion is measured with a 70 dB SPL input and may exceed the manufacturer's value by at most 3 percent.

cumleler.yazi: The tolerance is plus 3 decibels for equivalent input noise and plus 20 percent for battery current.
These values summarize the part of ANSI S3.22 used most often in the clinic.
cumleler.ses: These values summarize the part of ANSI S three point twenty two used most often in the clinic.

sahneler.metin: If an aid comes back sounding weak or crackly, first measure it in the test box and compare the result with its delivery measurement.
cumleler: A tip from the field: keep the pre-delivery test box measurement of every new aid in its file.
When the user complains that the sound has weakened or crackles, repeat the same measurement.
Reduced gain may point to a blocked receiver or microphone port; increased distortion may point to a weak battery or damaged receiver.
When comparing, make sure you measure with the same program, the same settings and adaptive features switched off.
This simple comparison prevents unnecessary fine-tuning and wrong referrals for repair.

maddeler.metin: OSPL90: output at 90 dB SPL input
THD and internal noise show quality

cumleler.yazi: In this lesson we saw that gain is found by subtracting the input level from the output level, and is summarized with the HFA.
cumleler.ses: In this lesson we saw that gain is found by subtracting the input level from the output level, and is summarized with the H F A.

cumleler.yazi: Maximum output is defined by the OSPL90 curve, measured with full-on gain and a 90 dB SPL input.
cumleler.ses: Maximum output is defined by the O S P L ninety curve, measured with full-on gain and a ninety decibel SPL input.

cumleler.yazi: The frequency range lies between the points where the response curve crosses the line 20 decibels below the HFA value.
cumleler.ses: The frequency range lies between the points where the response curve crosses the line twenty decibels below the H F A value.

cumleler: Harmonic distortion and equivalent input noise show the aid's sound quality and soundness.

sahneler.soru: HFA-OSPL90 is 116 dB SPL. Reference HFA gain?
sahneler.aciklama: Reference setting: HFA gain = HFA-OSPL90 minus _77 dB_; 116 minus 77 is 39 dB.

cumleler.yazi: Test yourself: an aid's HFA-OSPL90 is 116 dB SPL. About how many decibels is the HFA gain at the reference test setting?
cumleler.ses: Test yourself: an aid's H F A O S P L ninety is one hundred sixteen decibels SPL. About how many decibels is the H F A gain at the reference test setting?

cumleler: The correct answer is B: 39 decibels.

cumleler.yazi: At the reference setting, HFA gain is HFA-OSPL90 minus 77 decibels: 116 minus 77, which is 39 decibels.
cumleler.ses: At the reference setting, H F A gain is H F A O S P L ninety minus seventy seven decibels: one hundred sixteen minus seventy seven, which is thirty nine decibels.
